papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, delivering flickering light stimulation (FLS) during sleep deprivation prevented the upregulation of activity-dependent and unfolded protein response (UPR)/ER-stress genes while further increasing NREM slow-wave activity, and induced brief neuronal OFF periods resembling a sleep-like cortical state. The authors conclude that physiological manipulation of cortical activity can dissociate ER-stress molecular signatures from electrophysiological markers of sleep pressure.

papers.title: Neural circuitry mediating hypercapnia-induced microarousal and impaired sleep depth.
papers.summary: In a mouse model, intermittent hypercapnic air induced microarousals and reduced NREM sleep depth via activation of glutamatergic neurons in the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTSVglut2); projection-specific manipulations showed that NTSVglut2 inputs to the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), parabrachial nucleus, paraventricular thalamus, and locus coeruleus promote arousal, with PVN-projecting NTSVglut2 neurons monosynaptically activating PVN corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons to drive hypercapnia-induced arousal.

papers.title: ppGpp is present in, and functions to regulate sleep of, Drosophila.
papers.summary: Demonstrated that ppGpp is present in Drosophila and regulates sleep, with mesh1 mutants showing defective nighttime sleep and starvation-induced sleep loss rescued by wild-type but not catalytically inactive Mesh1; RelA expression phenocopied and Mesh1 overexpression reversed these phenotypes, implicating Dilp2 neurons in the pars intercerebralis.

papers.title: "Frontal Slow-Wave Asymmetry in Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Its Modulation During CPAP Titration".
papers.summary: In a retrospective study of 143 obstructive sleep apnea patients, CPAP titration reduced the apnea-hypopnea index and frontal delta power during N3 sleep, and attenuated interhemispheric slow-wave asymmetry, shifting dominance from right to left, suggesting that respiratory stabilization modulates cortical organization during deep sleep.

papers.title: Characterization of Sleep, Spectral, and Epileptiform Activity in Individuals Aged 8-27 Years with SYNGAP1-Related Disorder Using an at-Home Dry EEG Headband
papers.summary: Using an at-home dry-electrode EEG headband in a decentralized protocol, the study collected 180 recordings from 23 participants with SYNGAP1-related disorder, showing increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, altered sleep-stage distribution, and interictal epileptiform discharges in 22 of 23 participants. It also reproduced awake spectral abnormalities and revealed sleep-stage-dependent spectral biomarker dynamics.

papers.title: From labels to latents: revealing state-dependent hippocampal computations and non-spatial replay with Jump Latent Variable Model
papers.summary: Proposes the Jump Latent Variable Model, an unsupervised EM-based latent variable model that infers population-activity latents and whether their dynamics are continuous or fragmented, without external labels. Applied to rodent hippocampus, it identifies a cholinergic-modulated continuity-fragmentation axis across sleep-wake states, reveals position-independent population patterns missed by supervised spatial decoding, and uncovers prevalent non-spatial pre-play and post-task locomotor replay.

papers.title: Associations Between Biomarkers of Alzheimer's Disease and Sleep in Cognitively Unimpaired Older Adults.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: In 40 cognitively unimpaired older adults, examined associations between evening/morning plasma Alzheimer's biomarkers and polysomnographic sleep; higher t-tau and p-tau181 related to reduced N3 sleep and longer wakefulness, while amyloid-β measures associated most consistently with sleep microstructure, including shorter and less dense frontal sleep spindles.

papers.title: Sequential coupling of sleep oscillations enables concept-neuron reactivation and supports information flow across the human hippocampal-cortical circuit
papers.summary: Recording single-neuron activity in the medial temporal lobe of 10 epilepsy patients across 21 nights, the study found that sharp wave-ripple-locked firing revealed directed hippocampal-to-cortical information flow and selective reactivation of experience-dependent concept neurons. Cross-regional concept-cell co-activation was enhanced when hippocampal sharp wave-ripples coincided with cortical slow oscillation-spindle complexes.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms in health and disease.
papers.summary: This review discusses circadian rhythms regulated by core clock genes (e.g., BMAL1, CLOCK) and central pacemaker neurons, highlights how circadian disruption contributes to neurodegenerative, metabolic, and cardiovascular diseases and cancer via immune and cellular alterations, and outlines chronotherapy and personalized medicine approaches for aligning treatment with biological rhythms.

papers.title: Framework for combined functional and computational assessment of variant pathogenicity in the sodium leak channel NALCN.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.summary: The authors functionally characterized 19 variants of uncertain significance in the sodium leak channel NALCN using two-electrode voltage-clamp electrophysiology combined with computational protein stability and conservation scores, establishing a framework that distinguishes benign variants from gain- and loss-of-function variants and provides insight into NALCN channelopathy mechanisms.

papers.title: Advances in neurological disease models and optimization of the laboratory animal environment for reproducible research.
papers.summary: This review integrates advances in neurological disease models—ranging from genetic, molecular, and circuit phenotyping to primate translation—with evidence that husbandry and environmental variables such as microbiota, diet, housing, and enrichment are biological determinants of experimental outcomes. It argues that combining rigorous model characterization with evidence-based environmental control and transparent reporting will improve reproducibility and translational value.

papers.title: Longitudinal Sleep Spindle Maturation Trajectories and Their Association With Internalizing Problems in Adulthood.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal study of sleep spindles from childhood to young adulthood (N=28), slow spindle density declined with a posterior-to-anterior pattern, fast spindle density increased from childhood to adolescence then stabilized, and a steeper decline in slow spindle density from childhood to adolescence was associated with more internalizing problems in adulthood.

papers.title: Decoding Cell-level Circadian Phase and Rhythm-state Remodeling in Single-cell Transcriptomes With scRhythmBayes
papers.summary: The authors present scRhythmBayes, a probabilistic algorithm that combines a seed-gene count likelihood with a stratum-aware circular prior to infer cell-level circadian phase and assign posterior probabilities to rhythm-state categories in heterogeneous single-cell transcriptomes. It achieved higher phase-recovery accuracy than existing methods and revealed distinct phase occupancy and rhythm-state organization between periportal and pericentral hepatocytes and cell-type-selective temporal disorganization in human heart disease data.

papers.title: It's about time: modeling circadian regulation of cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmogenesis.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes computational models that incorporate circadian regulation into cardiac electrophysiology across sinoatrial nodal and ventricular myocytes, addressing pacemaking, arrhythmogenesis, and drug-induced proarrhythmic risk. It proposes a layered source-transfer-target framework and a current-level Hodgkin-Huxley formulation for circadian modulation of maximal conductance, channel gating, and ionic driving force, toward circadian-aware cardiac digital twins.

papers.title: Glycosides of Cistanche improve cognitive dysfunction in sleep-deprived model rats by activating the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
papers.summary: In a 21-day sleep-deprivation rat model, Cistanche glycosides improved Morris water maze performance, normalized sleep architecture, reduced oxidative stress, and preserved hippocampal CA1 neurons and synaptic proteins via activation of the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 pathway; these protective effects were abolished by the SIRT1 inhibitor EX527.

papers.title: Glymphatic Dysfunction Across Sleep Disorders and Its Cognitive Implications
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found significant glymphatic transport impairment in obstructive sleep apnea, with a moderate negative association between apnea-hypopnea index and DTI-ALPS index (r=-0.53), but did not find statistically significant glymphatic alterations in sleep deprivation or narcolepsy type 1.

papers.title: EEG-Captioner: Grounding EEG-to-Language Generation in Fundamental Signal Properties
papers.summary: The authors built an EEG-language dataset of 160,781 segments with signal-level QA pairs and feature-grounded captions, then introduced a Dual-Domain EEG Encoder and the EEG-Captioner framework, reaching 88.81% macro-balanced accuracy on signal-level QA and improving caption factual consistency from 82.06% to 83.46% over caption-only adaptation.

papers.title: Neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulation: A systematic review of task-based neuroimaging studies.
papers.summary: This preregistered systematic review synthesized 11 task-based fMRI studies of neural responses to food-related stimuli after experimental sleep deprivation or restriction. Across adult visual food-cue studies, sleep loss was generally associated with stronger activity in striatum, insula, anterior cingulate cortex, and inferior frontal gyrus, but effects were task-dependent and evidence was limited and heterogeneous.

papers.title: Acute creatine-guanidinoacetate supplementation improves regional brain oxygenation following sleep deprivation: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: A randomized controlled trial in 22 sleep-deprived young adults comparing acute creatine-guanidinoacetate, molecular hydrogen inhalation, caffeine, and placebo on regional brain oxygenation and attention. Creatine-GAA significantly increased frontal (50.8% to 61.0%) and temporal (63.1% to 70.2%) oxygen saturation but produced no significant between-group differences in attention-related outcomes.

papers.title: Impaired Dynamic Cerebral Autoregulation Across the REM Sleep Behavior Disorder Spectrum: Evidence From Isolated REM Sleep Without Atonia to Parkinson's Disease With RBD.
papers.summary: In a case-control study of iRSWA, iRBD, PD+RBD, and controls, dynamic cerebral autoregulation phase difference was significantly reduced across all patient groups and was associated with lower REM sleep amount and greater phasic RSWA, suggesting dCA impairment as an early feature of RBD-related neurodegeneration.

papers.title: EEG Edge-Centric Dynamics Reveal Distinct Post-Stroke Somatosensory Network Responses to Vibratory and Electrical Stimulation.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Using an edge-centric dynamic connectivity (ECDC) framework on EEG, this study compared whole-brain network responses to focal vibratory stimulation (FVS) versus neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) in 15 chronic stroke patients and 15 healthy controls. FVS in stroke participants produced shorter global theta-network latency, higher contralesional alpha network diversity, and reduced theta-alpha phase-amplitude coupling relative to NMES, providing interpretable network signatures for stimulation-specific brain responses.

papers.title: Decoding motor imagery EEG signals by a deep learning network integrating multiscale filtering and temporal-channel attention mechanisms.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a deep learning network combining multiscale parallel CNNs, Transformer blocks, and temporal-channel attention with a CNN classifier to decode motor imagery EEG. Using segmentation-reconstruction data augmentation, it achieved 80.21%, 90.19%, and 97.32% accuracy on three public BCI datasets, surpassing the strongest baselines by 2.59%, 1.27%, and 1.99%.

papers.title: Sleep in Different Types of Dizziness.
authors: Marco Antônio Sales Dantas de Lima
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 90 participants used 14-day actigraphy, home sleep apnea testing, and questionnaires to characterize sleep profiles in BPPV, vestibular migraine, and PPPD versus healthy controls. Each disorder showed a distinct signature: BPPV had sleep fragmentation and elevated AHI, PPPD showed high objective but poor subjective sleep quality, and VM had the shortest total sleep time with social jetlag.

papers.title: Noninvasive respiratory therapy: A physiology-oriented approach across acute, chronic, home, and palliative care settings.
papers.summary: This review reframes noninvasive respiratory therapy across acute, chronic, home, and palliative care around identifying the dominant physiological problem rather than the disease label. It details indications for noninvasive ventilation in acute hypercapnic COPD exacerbations and cardiogenic pulmonary edema, and emphasizes interface selection, leak control, humidification, synchrony, airway clearance, and monitoring for home support.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Rett Syndrome: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Explainable AI
papers.summary: This study compared PSD-based classical machine learning (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost) and end-to-end deep learning architectures on resting-state eyes-closed EEG for Rett syndrome classification using subject-wise cross-validation with balanced accuracy. Random Forest and EEGNet performed best, and SHAP and occlusion sensitivity analyses consistently identified delta and theta oscillations and centro-frontal regions as key discriminative biomarkers.

papers.title: Influence of chiropractic care on sleep-related behavior of athletic Mangalarga Marchador horses.
papers.summary: Nine athletic Mangalarga Marchador horses in an intensive system were observed over 72-hour periods before and after two chiropractic sessions, and resting behavior was compared. Chiropractic care was associated with reduced wakefulness time (p=0.003) and increased lateral recumbency time after both sessions (p=0.004), suggesting behavioral changes in sleep-related resting patterns.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
papers.summary: Reviews recent AI applications to intracranial EEG and stereo-EEG in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, covering epileptogenic zone localization, multimodal MRI integration, surgical planning, and iEEG-guided stimulation, while noting that most evidence remains retrospective and single-center without external validation.

papers.title: Perioperative Neurocognitive Disorders in Older Adults: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Evidence-Informed Management.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines mechanisms, candidate fluid biomarkers, and EEG features of perioperative neurocognitive disorders in older surgical adults, including neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, neurotransmitter imbalance, oxidative stress, and synaptic dysfunction. It concludes that multicomponent prevention and individualized anesthetic care remain the most defensible strategies, while EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure without consistently reducing postoperative delirium.

papers.title: Metabolic Dyshomeostasis, neuroinflammation, and glymphatic clearance deficits as convergent drivers of Alzheimer's disease: an exposome-based conceptual framework for prevention.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic evidence for an exposome-based model of sporadic Alzheimer's disease, proposing that metabolic dyshomeostasis, chronic neuroinflammation, and sleep/circadian disruption converge via shared molecular hubs (NF-κB, mTOR, ER stress) to lower the threshold for dementia. It identifies brain insulin resistance as central and argues for multi-domain prevention focused on the midlife vulnerability window, while noting causal human evidence for glymphatic clearance remains limited.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients
papers.summary: In the prospective ALADDIN cohort of 215 older non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery patients (168 with high-quality intraoperative EEG), lower anesthetic dose-adjusted frontoparietal EEG alpha power was linked to altered default mode, dorsal attention, and salience network connectivity and to reduced cortical thickness in occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices. Lower alpha power was also associated with postoperative ward delirium and greater delirium severity, suggesting a functional and structural basis for delirium risk.

papers.title: Home non-invasive ventilation in chronic respiratory failure: Evidence-based guidelines.
papers.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
papers.summary: These evidence-based guidelines provide consensus recommendations for initiating, titrating, and monitoring long-term home non-invasive ventilation across chronic respiratory failure etiologies, including COPD, neuromuscular disorders, obesity hypoventilation syndrome, and other conditions. Recommendations cover disease-specific patient selection, individualized ventilator settings, objective ventilation assessment, caregiver education, and structured follow-up.

papers.title: Trajectories of postoperative fatigue and their association with physical and mental health among patients with peritoneal metastases from colorectal and appendiceal cancer after cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy: a 1-year longitudinal study.
papers.summary: In a 1-year longitudinal study of 182 patients with peritoneal metastases from colorectal and appendiceal cancer after CRS-HIPEC, group-based trajectory modeling identified three postoperative fatigue trajectories: high-increasing (29.67%), moderate-increasing (37.36%), and low-increasing (31.87%). Poor sleep quality, inadequate pain management, and worse physical and mental conditions were linked to more severe fatigue trajectories, and the high-increasing group had significantly lower 12-month mental dimension scores.

papers.title: Circadian-Psychosocial Profiling of Cancer Pain: A Mixed-Methods Study on Heterogeneous Subgroups and Personalized Analgesic Efficacy.
papers.summary: This explanatory sequential mixed-methods study of 191 cancer pain inpatients used K-prototypes clustering of circadian, physiological, and psychosocial data to identify four subgroups with distinct analgesic responses. The high-melatonin cluster showed significant reductions in mean pain intensity and pain variability, whereas the elderly reverse-dipper cluster showed no significant analgesic effect, supporting multidimensional subtyping for individualized pain management.

papers.title: A proposed psychometabolic endotype of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: bidirectional interplay between psychological distress, eating dysfunction, sleep disruption, chronic stress, and metabolic deterioration.
papers.summary: This targeted narrative review proposes a candidate psychometabolic endotype of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (formerly PCOS) linking depression, anxiety, eating dysfunction, sleep disruption, chronic stress, and metabolic deterioration. It reports co-occurrence but notes mostly cross-sectional evidence, and cites one cohort finding that baseline depression/anxiety predicted incident metabolic syndrome over a median seven years (adjusted HR 1.45, 95% CI 1.02-2.06), supporting prognostic enrichment rather than causality.

papers.title: Characterizing Cancer Symptom Experiences and Related Psychosocial Concerns Through Chinese Social Media Narratives: Computational Text Analysis.
papers.summary: Computational text analysis of 26,086 Chinese social media posts using LLM annotation and BERTopic modeling found that 53.3% contained at least one SPPADE symptom, with pain most frequent (22.2%), and identified 13 latent psychosocial and experiential themes beyond standardized symptom domains.

papers.title: [Pseudo-remission in childhood absence epilepsy. Objective assessment of seizure control and the role of ethosuximide].
papers.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
papers.summary: This review examines pseudo-remission in childhood absence epilepsy, where caregivers and patients misjudge seizure control because typical absences are brief and parental observation is unreliable (sensitivity up to 43%). It recommends a three-minute hyperventilation test with attentional load and prolonged video-EEG for objective assessment, and reports Week 16 freedom-from-treatment-failure rates of 53% for ethosuximide, 58% for valproic acid, and 29% for lamotrigine (45%, 44%, 21% at Month 12).

papers.title: Exploratory data analysis and machine learning-based assessment of social media addiction and its impact on academic performance and mental health among students.
papers.summary: This study combined a literature review, dataset-driven exploratory data analysis, and correlational modeling on 705 participants from 110 countries to assess social media addiction among students and its links to mental health and academic performance. It reports strong associations between social media addiction and poorer sleep quality, worse mental health, and lower academic performance, with gender differences in usage and regional differences in platform preferences.

papers.title: NaV1.8 Inhibition and the Future of Nonopioid Analgesia in Otolaryngology: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes the pharmacology, efficacy, safety, limitations, and otolaryngology applications of suzetrigine, a first-in-class selective NaV1.8 inhibitor approved as a nonopioid analgesic. Across phase 2/3 trials in abdominoplasty and bunionectomy pain models involving more than 3000 patients, suzetrigine showed superior analgesia versus placebo and efficacy comparable to hydrocodone/acetaminophen, with adverse event rates similar to placebo and no significant respiratory, cardiac, or sedating effects.

papers.title: Rapid Improvement of Persistent Catatonia Temporally Associated With Amantadine After Benzodiazepine Intolerance and Discontinuation of Electroconvulsive Therapy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 23-year-old woman with schizophrenia-spectrum disorder and persistent catatonia who could not tolerate lorazepam or continue electroconvulsive therapy. After starting amantadine 100 mg twice daily, her Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale severity score fell from 11 to 3 within three days (a 72.7% reduction), with a final score of 2 after dose escalation and added zolpidem, though the authors note causal attribution is limited by confounders.

papers.title: Neuronal intermediate filament neurologic autoimmunity in a patient with Merkel cell carcinoma receiving pembrolizumab.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This case report describes a 55-year-old woman with stage IIIA Merkel cell carcinoma who developed vertigo, gait instability, dysarthria, and persistent right hemifacial and cervical spasms after pembrolizumab, with CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis and positive neuronal intermediate filament antibodies. Pembrolizumab was discontinued and she received high-dose corticosteroids followed by monthly intravenous immunoglobulin, with near-complete resolution of neurologic symptoms after 6 months.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
